items.quote: The next day the people of Shechem went out to the fields, and this was reported to Abimelek.
items.contrast: The reported movement into the fields prompted the ambush; seeing people coming out of the city happened afterward.
items.reason: “This” refers to the people going out to the fields, and “So” connects that report to Abimelek’s decision to set the ambush. The question clearly tests the trigger rather than his later observation.

items.quote: Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
items.contrast: The seven sons are the beaten victims who flee; the man with the evil spirit is the attacker.
items.reason: The plural pronouns “them” and “they” continue to refer to the seven sons, while the singular “he” is the man who attacks them. Resolving those roles is necessary to answer correctly.

items.quote: Some time later, Ben-Hadad king of Aram mobilized his entire army and marched up and laid siege to Samaria.
items.contrast: Ben-Hadad mobilizes his army before marching up and laying siege to Samaria.
items.reason: The coordinated actions are presented in chronological order, so mobilizing the army is unambiguously first. The question tests the sequence rather than merely identifying an action.

items.quote: God helped him against the Philistines and against the Arabs who lived in Gur Baal and against the Meunites.
items.contrast: The Philistines, Arabs, and Meunites are opponents against whom God helps Uzziah; the Ammonites are instead described as bringing tribute.
items.reason: The repeated phrase “against” explicitly identifies all three opponent groups. Distinguishing them from the separately mentioned Ammonites requires tracking the groups’ different relationships to Uzziah.

items.quote: For I was commanded by the word of the Lord: ‘You must not eat bread or drink water or return by the way you came.’
items.contrast: The Lord’s command causes the refusal; the offer of half the king’s possessions is a hypothetical concession, not the reason.
items.reason: “For” introduces the man’s stated reason, while “even if” shows that a larger offer would not change his refusal. The question tests that causal and concessive relationship.
